title: Art & Architecture of Medieval India
desc: Indo-Islamic and Mughal art, architecture, painting

basic.q: Who commenced the construction of the Qutub Minar in Delhi?
basic.e: Qutb-ud-din Aibak began construction of the Qutub Minar; it was completed by his successor Iltutmish, who added three more storeys.

basic.q: The Alai Darwaza, known for introducing true arch and dome construction in India, was built by which ruler?
basic.e: Alauddin Khalji built the Alai Darwaza as the entrance to the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque; it is considered the first structure in India to use genuine arch-and-dome technique with radiating voussoirs.

basic.q: Humayun's Tomb, the first Mughal garden-tomb in India, was built under the patronage of whom?
basic.e: Haji Begum, Humayun's widow, commissioned the tomb; it was designed by Persian architect Mirak Mirza Ghiyas and set the template for the charbagh garden-tomb tradition culminating in the Taj Mahal.

basic.q: Fatehpur Sikri, built as a new capital city, was constructed by which Mughal emperor?
basic.e: Akbar built Fatehpur Sikri near Agra in honour of Sufi saint Shaikh Salim Chishti; it served as the Mughal capital for about 14 years.

basic.q: The Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri was constructed by Akbar to commemorate which event?
basic.e: The Buland Darwaza ('Gate of Magnificence') was built by Akbar to mark his conquest of Gujarat in 1573.

basic.q: The Taj Mahal was built by Shah Jahan in memory of whom?
basic.e: Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal as a mausoleum for his wife Mumtaz Mahal; the chief architect is traditionally identified as Ustad Ahmad Lahori.

basic.q: The Red Fort at Delhi was built by which Mughal ruler as part of his new capital Shahjahanabad?
basic.e: Shah Jahan built the Red Fort (Lal Qila) as the palace-fort of his new capital Shahjahanabad.

basic.q: The legendary musician Tansen, credited with creating several ragas, adorned the court of which emperor?
basic.e: Tansen was one of the 'Navratnas' (nine jewels) in Akbar's court and is credited with ragas such as Miyan ki Malhar and Miyan ki Todi.

basic.q: Which two Persian master-painters, brought to India by Humayun, laid the foundation of the Mughal school of painting?
o: Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad
basic.e: Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad accompanied Humayun back from Persia and trained Indian artists, establishing the Mughal atelier later expanded under Akbar.

basic.q: The Hamzanama, an illustrated manuscript of over 1400 large paintings produced over roughly 15 years, was commissioned by which emperor?
basic.e: The Hamzanama (Story of Amir Hamza) was commissioned by Akbar and is one of the largest illustrated manuscript projects of Mughal painting.

basic.q: The Mughal painter Ustad Mansur, celebrated for his naturalistic studies of birds and animals such as the Siberian crane, flourished in whose reign?
basic.e: Ustad Mansur was the leading natural-history painter under Jahangir, who took a personal interest in flora and fauna studies.

basic.q: The Padshahnama, a richly illustrated official chronicle depicting courtly and military events, was prepared during the reign of which emperor?
basic.e: The Padshahnama is an illustrated official history of the reign of Shah Jahan.

basic.q: Which of the following is a well-known Rajput (Rajasthani) school of miniature painting?
basic.e: Mewar (along with Bundi, Kishangarh, Marwar) is one of the principal schools of Rajasthani/Rajput miniature painting, distinct from later Company or Tanjore styles.

basic.q: Bishandas, renowned for his skill in portrait painting, was specially deputed by Jahangir to accompany an embassy to which region?
basic.e: Jahangir sent the painter Bishandas with an embassy to the Safavid Persian court to portray Shah Abbas I.

basic.q: The provincial Indo-Islamic style of Bengal is particularly known for the use of which distinctive architectural feature, derived from local hut forms?
basic.e: Bengal's provincial style, seen in structures like the Adina Mosque at Pandua, adapted the curved 'chala' roof form of Bengali thatched huts, along with terracotta ornamentation.

basic.q: The Jama Masjid at Ahmedabad, notable for blending indigenous temple-style elements such as carved pillars with Islamic forms, belongs to which provincial style?
basic.e: The Gujarat provincial style is marked by the incorporation of local Jain/Hindu temple craftsmanship (carved pillars, toranas) into mosque architecture, as seen at Ahmedabad's Jama Masjid.

basic.q: The Jahaz Mahal and Hindola Mahal, notable examples of provincial Indo-Islamic architecture, are located at which site?
basic.e: Mandu in Malwa is home to the Jahaz Mahal (Ship Palace) and Hindola Mahal (Swinging Palace), key examples of the Malwa provincial style.

basic.q: The Gol Gumbaz, famous for its whispering gallery and one of the largest single-chamber domes in the world, was built as the mausoleum of which ruler?
basic.e: The Gol Gumbaz at Bijapur is the mausoleum of Mohammed Adil Shah and represents the mature Deccani (Bijapur) style of Indo-Islamic architecture.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements about the Qutub Minar complex: 1. The Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque adjacent to it was built using material obtained from demolished Hindu and Jain temples. 2. The Alai Darwaza represents the first genuine use of arch-and-dome technique in India. 3. Iltutmish built the entire five-storeyed Qutub Minar in a single reign. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false: construction began under Qutb-ud-din Aibak and continued under Iltutmish; the tower reached its present form only after later repairs (Firoz Shah Tughlaq rebuilt the top storeys after lightning damage).

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Iltutmish's tomb at the Qutub complex uses a true arch with voussoirs and a keystone. 2. Early Delhi Sultanate structures largely employed the corbelled (false) arch and dome technique inherited from indigenous trabeate tradition. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 2 is correct: early Sultanate buildings, including Iltutmish's tomb, used the corbelled/false arch (horizontal courses stepped inward), not a true radiating arch; hence statement 1 is incorrect.

intermediate.q: With reference to Humayun's Tomb, consider the following statements: 1. It was the first Mughal structure to use a charbagh (four-part) garden layout on a monumental scale. 2. It was built entirely of white marble. 3. Its architect was of Persian origin. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong — the tomb is built of red sandstone with white marble inlay/dome, not entirely marble.

intermediate.q: Consider the following pairs of Mughal monuments and their patrons: 1. Buland Darwaza - Akbar. 2. Red Fort - Shah Jahan. 3. Taj Mahal - Jahangir. How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
intermediate.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. The Taj Mahal was built by Shah Jahan, not Jahangir, so pair 3 is incorrect.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements regarding Mughal painting: 1. Under Akbar, Persian and Indian painters worked together on large-scale illustrated manuscripts. 2. Jahangir's reign is particularly noted for naturalistic studies of flora and fauna and refined portraiture. 3. Under Aurangzeb, imperial patronage of painting expanded significantly compared to Shah Jahan's reign. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false — Aurangzeb, due to his orthodox outlook, sharply curtailed royal patronage of painting, causing many artists to migrate to provincial/Rajput courts.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Kishangarh school of Rajput painting is famous for the 'Bani Thani' portrait style. 2. The Bundi school is known for its depiction of hunting scenes and court life against lush landscapes. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements correctly describe distinguishing features of the Kishangarh and Bundi schools of Rajasthani painting respectively.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements about provincial Indo-Islamic architectural styles: 1. The Bengal style used curved cornices imitating bamboo hut roofs. 2. The Jaunpur (Sharqi) style is known for its massive propylon (screen) facades on mosques. 3. The Deccan style under the Bahmanis and their successors shows strong Persian influence, including glazed tilework. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: All three statements accurately describe regional variations: Bengal's curved roofs, Jaunpur's distinctive propylon facades (e.g., Atala Masjid), and the Deccan's Persian-influenced glazed tile ornamentation (e.g., Gol Gumbaz, Ibrahim Rauza).

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Fatehpur Sikri's Panch Mahal is a five-storeyed pillared pavilion with no use of arches. 2. The Jodha Bai Palace at Fatehpur Sikri shows a blend of Hindu and Islamic architectural motifs. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct: the Panch Mahal is a trabeate (arch-less) columned structure, and the Jodha Bai Palace combines Hindu temple-derived brackets and chhatris with Islamic layout principles.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements regarding the Taj Mahal: 1. Its calligraphic inscriptions were executed by Amanat Khan Shirazi. 2. Pietra dura (inlay of semi-precious stones) was used extensively in its decoration. 3. It was declared complete within five years of the start of construction. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — the mausoleum took about 12 years for the main structure (the overall complex took around 20 years).

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements about music and painting under the Mughals: 1. Tansen served in Akbar's court as one of the Navratnas. 2. Miyan Tansen is credited with composing the raga 'Miyan ki Todi'. 3. Tansen's original name before joining Akbar's court was Ramtanu Pandey. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: All three statements are historically accepted: Tansen (born Ramtanu Pandey) was among Akbar's Navratnas and is credited with ragas including Miyan ki Todi and Miyan ki Malhar.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Charminar at Hyderabad was built by the Qutb Shahi ruler Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah. 2. It was constructed to commemorate the founding of the city of Hyderabad. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct; the Charminar (1591) was built by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah to mark the founding of Hyderabad, reportedly also to commemorate the end of a plague.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Arhai-din-ka-Jhonpra at Ajmer was originally a Sanskrit college converted into a mosque. 2. It displays a screen of arches added in front of a pillared hall reused from an earlier structure. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct; the Arhai-din-ka-Jhonpra was converted from a Sanskrit pathshala/temple complex, with a Sultanate-period arched screen added to its facade.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Sheikh Salim Chishti's tomb at Fatehpur Sikri is built of white marble with intricate jali (lattice) screens. 2. It is set within the same courtyard as the Buland Darwaza and Jama Masjid. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements correctly describe the tomb of the Sufi saint Salim Chishti, located within the Jama Masjid courtyard at Fatehpur Sikri, celebrated for its marble lattice screens.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Ibrahim Rauza at Bijapur is the tomb of Ibrahim Adil Shah II. 2. It is often considered among the structures whose design influenced the garden-tomb concept later refined in the Taj Mahal. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are broadly accepted; the Ibrahim Rauza, a Bijapur (Deccan) garden tomb, is often cited among the structures whose design elements anticipate features refined later in the Taj Mahal.

intermediate.q: Which of the following pairs of medieval Indian monument and its architectural distinguishing feature is NOT correctly matched?
o: Qutub Minar - Tapering fluted tower with balconies
Alai Darwaza - True arch and dome
Taj Mahal - Pietra dura inlay work
intermediate.e: The Gol Gumbaz is celebrated for its massive single unsupported dome and whispering gallery, not a charbagh garden layout, which is a hallmark of Mughal tomb architecture like Humayun's Tomb and the Taj Mahal.

intermediate.q: Arrange the following in chronological order of construction: 1. Alai Darwaza 2. Humayun's Tomb 3. Qutub Minar 4. Taj Mahal
intermediate.e: Chronological order: Qutub Minar (early 13th c.) then Alai Darwaza (early 14th c.) then Humayun's Tomb (mid-16th c.) then Taj Mahal (mid-17th c.).

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Daswanth and Basawan were notable Indian-origin painters trained in Akbar's atelier. 2. The Mughal school of painting under Akbar largely rejected European artistic influence. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct - Daswanth and Basawan were leading Indian painters under Akbar. Statement 2 is false, as Akbar's atelier actively absorbed European techniques such as perspective and chiaroscuro introduced through Jesuit missions.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Sheesh Mahal (Hall of Mirrors) technique using inlaid glass pieces is associated with later Mughal and Rajput palace decoration. 2. The Diwan-i-Khas at Fatehpur Sikri contains a uniquely carved central pillar supporting a circular platform. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct: Sheesh Mahal decoration using mirror/glass inlay spread in later Mughal and Rajput palaces, and Fatehpur Sikri's Diwan-i-Khas has a distinctive central carved pillar with radiating stone brackets supporting Akbar's platform.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque's screen of arches added by Iltutmish shows corbelled arches rather than true voussoired arches. 2. The true radiating arch became a standard feature of Delhi Sultanate architecture only from the Khalji period onward. 3. The Tughlaq architectural style is marked by austerity, using sloping (batter) walls and a combination arch-and-lintel (trabeate-cum-arcuate) system. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: All three statements are correct. Iltutmish-era screens still relied on corbelling; the true arch became standard only from Khalji times; and the Tughlaq style is known for sloping walls and a hybrid arch-lintel system reflecting austerity and speed of construction.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The double dome technique, allowing a taller external dome without an overly high internal chamber, was fully developed in Mughal architecture by the time of the Taj Mahal. 2. Humayun's Tomb already exhibits an early example of the double dome. 3. The dome of Gol Gumbaz at Bijapur is a single-shell dome, not a double dome. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: All three are correct: the double-dome technique matured by the Taj Mahal, appeared earlier at Humayun's Tomb, while the Gol Gumbaz uniquely uses a single massive shell dome rather than a double dome.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements about the Panch Mahal at Fatehpur Sikri: 1. It has five storeys, each smaller than the one below, culminating in a single-pillared kiosk. 2. It was designed for use by the royal ladies, screened by carved stone jalis. 3. It employs true arches on each storey. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct - the Panch Mahal is a five-storeyed pyramidal pavilion likely used by royal women with jali screens. Statement 3 is false, since the Panch Mahal is a purely trabeate (post-and-lintel) structure with no arches.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The term 'Indo-Islamic' architecture refers to a style that mechanically combined Islamic forms with Hindu forms without mutual adaptation. 2. Indian craftsmen contributed decorative motifs such as lotus and bell-and-chain patterns to Sultanate-period mosques. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 2 is correct - motifs like the lotus and bell-and-chain were adapted from indigenous temple craft into mosque decoration. Statement 1 is incorrect, as Indo-Islamic architecture represents genuine synthesis and mutual adaptation, not mechanical combination.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements regarding provincial/regional Sultanate styles: 1. The Sharqi rulers of Jaunpur are known for grand propylon (pylon-like) mosque gateways, as in the Atala Masjid. 2. The Bahmani style at Gulbarga shows early Persian influence, seen in the Jama Masjid built without a central open courtyard. 3. The Vijayanagara style, though contemporaneous, is generally classified as a continuation of Dravidian Hindu temple architecture rather than Indo-Islamic style. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: All three statements are accurate: Jaunpur's massive gateway facades, the courtyard-less Gulbarga Jama Masjid reflecting Persian-inspired design, and Vijayanagara's continuation of Dravidian temple tradition alongside some Islamic decorative borrowings (e.g., Lotus Mahal) are well documented.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Jahangir's autobiography, the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri, records his personal interest in natural history illustrated by court painters. 2. Ustad Mansur was given the title 'Nadir-ul-Asr' (Wonder of the Age) for his paintings of flora and fauna. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct: Jahangir's memoir records his naturalist interests, and he conferred the title Nadir-ul-Asr on Ustad Mansur for his exceptional studies of birds and animals.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. European artistic techniques such as linear perspective and chiaroscuro entered Mughal painting through Jesuit missionaries at Akbar's court. 2. Basawan is credited with pioneering the use of foreshortening and a low horizon line in Mughal miniatures. 3. Portraiture as a distinct genre in Mughal painting reached its peak under Akbar rather than Jahangir. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong - individual portraiture reached its zenith under Jahangir, who prized naturalistic, individualized likenesses over Akbar's more narrative-manuscript focus.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements about Rajput painting: 1. The Pahari sub-schools (e.g., Basohli, Kangra) developed distinct styles within the hill states of the Himalayan foothills. 2. The Basohli style is noted for bold colours and the use of beetle-wing cases to depict jewellery. 3. The Kangra style is associated with softer lyricism, often depicting Krishna-Radha themes. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: All three statements are correct descriptions of Pahari painting sub-schools: Basohli's bold palette with beetle-wing inlay, and Kangra's lyrical Vaishnava themes, both flourishing in the Himalayan hill states.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The charbagh layout symbolically represents the Quranic conception of paradise divided into four quadrants by water channels. 2. Babur is credited with introducing the charbagh garden form to India. 3. The charbagh at Humayun's Tomb is the earliest surviving large-scale example integrated with a monumental tomb structure in India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: All three statements are correct: the charbagh's fourfold division has Quranic paradisiac symbolism, Babur introduced it to India (e.g., Ram Bagh, Agra), and Humayun's Tomb is the earliest surviving instance combining it monumentally with a tomb.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Taj Mahal complex includes a mosque and a jawab (mirror-image structure) flanking the mausoleum for architectural symmetry. 2. The jawab at the Taj Mahal also functions as a mosque, unlike the actual mosque, since it faces away from Mecca. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct: the jawab ('answer') building mirrors the mosque for symmetry but cannot be a functioning mosque, since, unlike the actual mosque, it does not face Mecca (west).

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Akbar's tomb at Sikandra was completed under the supervision of Jahangir. 2. It departs from the charbagh-with-central-dome format by having no dome at all over the main cenotaph chamber. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct: Akbar's tomb, begun in his lifetime, was completed by Jahangir, and unusually its topmost storey open cenotaph is uncovered without a dome.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Moti Masjid inside the Red Fort was built by Aurangzeb for his personal use. 2. It is constructed entirely of white marble, unlike the predominantly red sandstone structures of Shah Jahan's Red Fort. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct: the Moti Masjid (Pearl Mosque) within the Red Fort was added by Aurangzeb and built of white marble, contrasting with the red sandstone predominant in Shah Jahan's structures.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Charminar at Hyderabad has four grand arches opening in four directions supporting four minarets. 2. It predates the construction of the Taj Mahal. 3. It was built under Bahmani patronage. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct (built 1591, before the Taj Mahal of the 1630s-40s). Statement 3 is wrong - it was built by the Qutb Shahi dynasty of Golconda, not the Bahmanis, who had already fragmented into successor states by then.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Ibadat Khana built by Akbar at Fatehpur Sikri was originally intended as a hall for debate among Muslim theologians. 2. It later hosted representatives of Hindu, Jain, Zoroastrian and Christian faiths as well. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct: the Ibadat Khana began as a forum for Islamic theological debate and was later opened to scholars of other faiths, feeding into Akbar's syncretic ideas culminating in Din-i-Ilahi.

advanced.q: With reference to the evolution of the Sultanate 'Imperial Style', consider the following statements: 1. The Slave (Mamluk) dynasty phase relied heavily on reused temple spolia. 2. The Khalji phase introduced true arches, domes, and use of red sandstone with marble decoration together for the first time on a large scale. 3. The Tughlaq phase is associated with a shift toward grey stone rubble masonry and plastered surfaces due to resource constraints. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: All three statements correctly trace the stylistic evolution: Mamluk-era spolia reuse, Khalji innovations in arch/dome and stone combination, and Tughlaq austerity using cheaper rubble masonry with plaster finishing.

advanced.q: Assertion (A): The Alai Darwaza is considered architecturally more advanced than the earliest storeys of the Qutub Minar. Reason (R): The Alai Darwaza employs a true arch with a keystone, while the earliest storeys of the Qutub Minar rely on corbelled construction. Which of the following is correct?
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
advanced.e: Both are true and R correctly explains A - the Alai Darwaza's genuine radiating arch with keystone marks a technological advance over the corbelled construction of Aibak's original Qutub Minar phase.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Mumtaz Mahal's original name was Arjumand Banu Begum. 2. She died in Burhanpur (Deccan) during childbirth, after which her body was later moved to Agra for interment in the Taj Mahal. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct: Arjumand Banu Begum (Mumtaz Mahal) died at Burhanpur in 1631 during the birth of her 14th child, and her remains were later transferred to Agra for the Taj Mahal.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Gol Gumbaz's whispering gallery allows even a faint sound to be heard clearly across the chamber due to the dome's acoustic properties. 2. Its dome rests on interlocking pendentive-like arches rather than a drum with a peristyle, a technique distinct from the Taj Mahal's dome support system. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct: the Gol Gumbaz dome's unique acoustics create the famous whispering gallery effect, and its structural support uses intersecting arches (a distinct engineering solution) compared to the drum-and-dome system of the Taj Mahal.

title: Economic Impact of British Rule
desc: Colonial drain, land revenue and deindustrialization

basic.q: Who propounded the 'Drain of Wealth' theory, arguing that a significant part of India's wealth was being transferred to Britain without adequate economic return?
basic.e: Dadabhai Naoroji propounded the Drain of Wealth theory, most fully elaborated in his book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901).

basic.q: The Permanent Settlement of land revenue in Bengal, Bihar and Odisha was introduced in 1793 by which Governor-General?
basic.e: Lord Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement (Zamindari System) in 1793, fixing land revenue demand in perpetuity.

basic.q: The Ryotwari system of land revenue, under which settlement was made directly with the individual cultivator, was mainly implemented in which regions?
basic.e: The Ryotwari system, associated with Thomas Munro and Alexander Read, was mainly implemented in the Madras and Bombay Presidencies.

basic.q: The Mahalwari system of land revenue settlement was based on which unit of assessment?
o: The zamindar's entire estate in perpetuity
basic.e: Under the Mahalwari system, introduced in the North-Western Provinces and Punjab, revenue was assessed on the village/estate (mahal) as a unit, with joint responsibility of the village community.

basic.q: Romesh Chunder Dutt, an early Indian economic nationalist, is best known for authoring which work?
o: Poverty and Un-British Rule in India
Rise and Growth of Economic Nationalism in India
basic.e: R.C. Dutt authored 'The Economic History of India' (in two volumes), providing a detailed critique of British economic policy.

basic.q: Mahadev Govind Ranade, regarded as a founder of economic nationalism in India, was closely associated with which organisation?
basic.e: M.G. Ranade was closely associated with the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha and advocated state-aided industrialization.

basic.q: The term 'deindustrialization' in the context of colonial India primarily refers to which phenomenon?
o: Decline of traditional Indian handicrafts and artisanal industries
Growth of the railway manufacturing sector
basic.e: Deindustrialization refers to the decline of India's traditional handicraft industries (notably textiles) due to competition from machine-made British goods and discriminatory tariff policy.

basic.q: The decline of which famous textile industry is frequently cited as a classic example of deindustrialization under British rule?
basic.e: The decline of Dacca muslin, once famed worldwide, is the most cited example of deindustrialization, as cheaper machine-made Lancashire cloth flooded Indian markets.

basic.q: The first Famine Commission, appointed after the devastating famine of 1876-78, was headed by whom?
basic.e: The Famine Commission of 1880 was headed by Richard Strachey, and it recommended the Famine Code among other measures.

basic.q: The first passenger railway line in India, opened in 1853, ran between which two places?
basic.e: India's first passenger railway line ran between Bombay and Thane (1853), operated by the Great Indian Peninsula Railway.

basic.q: 'Home Charges', a key component of the Drain of Wealth, referred to payments made by the Government of India in Britain for which of the following?
o: Only the salaries of Indian civil servants
Interest on public debt raised in England, pensions and salaries of British officials, and India Office expenses
Only military expenditure incurred within India
Only railway construction costs within India
basic.e: Home Charges included interest on debt raised in England, pensions/furlough allowances of British officials, and costs of administering the India Office in London - all paid out of Indian revenues.

basic.q: The 'tinkathia' system, under which peasants were compelled to grow indigo on a fixed portion of their land, was prevalent in which region?
basic.e: The tinkathia system (compulsory indigo cultivation on 3/20th of landholding) prevailed in Champaran, Bihar, and became the site of Gandhi's first satyagraha in India in 1917.

basic.q: Which of the following was a key feature of the Permanent Settlement of 1793?
o: The revenue demand was revised every 30 years
Settlement was made directly with the cultivator, not the zamindar
The land revenue demand was fixed in perpetuity
It applied uniformly across all British Indian territories
basic.e: Under the Permanent Settlement, the revenue demand from zamindars was fixed forever ('permanently'), unlike Ryotwari and Mahalwari, which allowed periodic revision.

basic.q: Under the Ryotwari system, the revenue assessment on land was:
o: Collected only from zamindars, not cultivators
Abolished after the Charter Act of 1833
basic.e: Unlike the Permanent Settlement, Ryotwari assessments were periodically revised, allowing the state to raise demand as agricultural conditions/prices changed.

basic.q: Dadabhai Naoroji achieved which distinction in British politics?
o: He became the first Indian member of the British House of Lords
He was the first Indian Governor of Bombay
He became the first Indian elected to the British House of Commons
He was the first Indian to address the UN General Assembly
basic.e: Dadabhai Naoroji was elected to the British House of Commons in 1892 from Finsbury Central, becoming the first Indian MP.

basic.q: The Deccan Riots of 1875, in which peasants attacked moneylenders' account books and property, were primarily a reaction to which phenomenon?
o: The imposition of the Permanent Settlement in the Deccan
Rising agrarian indebtedness linked to commercialization of agriculture
The introduction of the Ryotwari system for the first time
A sudden abolition of land revenue
basic.e: The Deccan Riots (1875) reflected peasant anger at exploitative moneylenders amid growing indebtedness linked to commercialization of agriculture (especially cotton cultivation).

basic.q: 'Commercialization of agriculture' under British rule chiefly refers to which trend?
o: A shift from cash-crop cultivation to subsistence farming
Government purchase of all agricultural produce at fixed prices
A shift from subsistence food-grain cultivation toward cash crops for market/export
basic.e: Commercialization of agriculture involved a shift toward growing cash crops (cotton, jute, indigo, opium, tea) for market sale and export rather than purely for local subsistence.

basic.q: Nationalist critics argued that British investment in Indian railways primarily served which purpose?
o: Providing free transport for Indian pilgrims
Facilitating export of Indian raw materials and import of British manufactures, besides strategic/military needs
basic.e: Nationalists like R.C. Dutt argued railways mainly served British commercial and strategic interests - facilitating raw material exports and finished-goods imports - while burdening Indian taxpayers through the 'guarantee system'.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Under the Permanent Settlement, zamindars became owners of land with a fixed, unchanging revenue obligation to the state. 2. Under the Mahalwari system, the revenue demand was periodically revisable and settlement was made village-wise. 3. Under the Ryotwari system, the state recognized zamindars as intermediaries between it and the cultivator. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong - the defining feature of Ryotwari was the absence of zamindar intermediaries, with the state settling revenue directly with the individual cultivator (ryot).

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements regarding Dadabhai Naoroji's Drain Theory: 1. It held that a part of India's national wealth was being exported to Britain without adequate commercial or material return. 2. It included Home Charges, remittances of salaries/pensions of European officials, and profits repatriated by British capital as components of the drain. 3. Naoroji estimated that the drain had no measurable negative impact on India's capital formation. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 contradicts the theory itself - Naoroji argued the drain impoverished India by starving it of capital that could otherwise have been invested domestically.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. R.C. Dutt's critique focused heavily on the impact of land revenue policy and free trade on India's agrarian economy. 2. Naoroji's analysis was primarily statistical, estimating national income and the magnitude of the drain. 3. Both Dutt and Naoroji supported continuation of laissez-faire free trade policy as beneficial for India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statements 1 and 2 correctly characterize the two economists' distinct emphases. Statement 3 is false - both were critical of one-sided free trade that favoured British manufactures while exposing Indian industry to unequal competition.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements about deindustrialization: 1. It was accelerated by discriminatory tariff policy that kept Indian import duties low on British goods while Indian exports faced tariffs in Britain. 2. It led to increased pressure on land as displaced artisans turned to agriculture. 3. It resulted in an overall decline in India's population dependent on agriculture. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is the opposite of what happened - deindustrialization actually increased the proportion of population dependent on agriculture, not decreased it, as displaced artisans had few alternatives.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The 'guarantee system' for railway construction assured British investors a minimum rate of return, funded if necessary from Indian revenues. 2. Railways in India were primarily built with routes optimized for the convenience of Indian internal trade rather than export-import trade or troop movement. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct - under the guarantee system, the government assured British companies a fixed return (commonly around 5%), met from Indian taxes if profits fell short. Statement 2 is incorrect, as routes were largely designed to link ports with raw-material-producing hinterlands and serve strategic/military movement.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements regarding famines under colonial rule: 1. The Famine Commission of 1880 recommended the drafting of a Famine Code. 2. British 'laissez-faire' orthodoxy often delayed state relief intervention during famines. 3. The Great Famine of 1876-78 primarily affected only the princely states and not British-administered provinces. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false - the 1876-78 famine severely affected British-administered Madras and Bombay Presidencies as well as some princely states such as Mysore.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Champaran indigo system (tinkathia) compelled cultivators to grow indigo on a fixed share of their holding for the planter. 2. Gandhi's Champaran Satyagraha (1917) was primarily directed against this indigo cultivation system. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements correctly describe the tinkathia system and its role as the immediate grievance behind Gandhi's Champaran Satyagraha.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements comparing the three major land revenue systems: 1. Permanent Settlement created a class of zamindars with proprietary rights over land. 2. Ryotwari conferred proprietary rights directly upon cultivators, subject to timely revenue payment. 3. Mahalwari recognized the village community/headman as jointly responsible for revenue payment. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: All three statements accurately capture the structural differences between the Permanent Settlement, Ryotwari, and Mahalwari systems in terms of who held rights/responsibility for revenue.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Commercialization of agriculture increased Indian peasants' exposure to global price fluctuations. 2. It was accompanied by rising rural indebtedness to moneylenders. 3. It uniformly improved the standard of living of small peasants across India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false - commercialization frequently worsened conditions for small/marginal peasants, who bore price risk and debt burdens without proportionate gains.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Naoroji served as President of the Indian National Congress on more than one occasion. 2. He was a member of the British Liberal Party when elected to Parliament. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct: Naoroji presided over the Indian National Congress in 1886, 1893 and 1906, and he was elected to the British Parliament as a Liberal Party candidate.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Under the Permanent Settlement, the state's revenue share from zamindars was fixed, but zamindars remained free to raise rents from tenants. 2. In practice, most zamindars used this surplus mainly for productive agricultural investment rather than as rentier income. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect - most zamindars historically functioned as rentiers, extracting rising rents without corresponding investment in agricultural improvement, a key criticism of the Permanent Settlement.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The drain of wealth, according to Naoroji, could be reduced by increasing Indian representation in the civil services to cut down on remittances of high salaries to Britain. 2. Naoroji also called for greater Indianization of the army as a remedial measure. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements correctly reflect Naoroji's proposed remedies - Indianization of civil services and the army - to reduce the outflow of salaries, pensions and allowances constituting Home Charges.

intermediate.q: Arrange the following land revenue systems in the chronological order of their introduction: 1. Mahalwari Settlement 2. Permanent Settlement 3. Ryotwari Settlement
intermediate.e: Chronologically: Permanent Settlement (1793) came first, followed by the Ryotwari settlement (from early 1800s in Madras), and then the Mahalwari system (from 1822 onward in North-Western Provinces).

intermediate.q: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched (revenue system - region of predominant application)?
intermediate.e: Mahalwari was mainly applied in the North-Western Provinces, Punjab and parts of Central India - not Madras, which was primarily under the Ryotwari system.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Opium was a major commercialized crop exported from India to China under British encouragement, forming part of colonial trade balance strategy. 2. Indigo cultivation was entirely voluntary for Bengal peasants throughout the 19th century, with no element of compulsion. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct - opium exports to China helped offset Britain's trade deficit. Statement 2 is false, as Bengal indigo cultivation involved considerable coercion of ryots by planters, famously protested in the 'Indigo Revolt' of 1859-60 and depicted in 'Neel Darpan'.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Indigo Revolt of 1859-60 in Bengal was directed against European planters' coercive cultivation practices. 2. It led to the appointment of an Indigo Commission by the colonial government. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct: the Indigo Revolt (1859-60) targeted planter coercion, and it resulted in an official Indigo Commission of inquiry.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. British trade policy after the Industrial Revolution reversed India's traditional export profile from finished textiles to raw materials such as raw cotton and jute. 2. This reversal is cited by nationalist economists as clear evidence of a colonial economic relationship benefiting Britain's industrial base. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct and represent the core nationalist critique - India shifted from being an exporter of manufactured textiles to a supplier of raw materials feeding British industry, importing back finished goods.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Under the Ryotwari system, the government dealt directly with millions of individual peasant proprietors, increasing its administrative burden compared to Permanent Settlement. 2. Thomas Munro is closely associated with the introduction and defense of the Ryotwari system in Madras. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct: Ryotwari's direct dealings with numerous peasants raised administrative costs, and Thomas Munro was its chief architect and advocate in Madras.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Permanent Settlement was expected by Cornwallis to encourage zamindars to invest in agricultural improvement due to assured fixed revenue. 2. In practice, many original zamindari estates were auctioned off for revenue default in the early 19th century, leading to the rise of new absentee landlords. 3. The 'Sunset Law' allowed for auctioning zamindari estates that failed to pay revenue by a fixed deadline. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: All three statements are correct: Cornwallis's original rationale, the resulting large-scale auctions of defaulting estates under the so-called 'Sunset Law', and the emergence of new, often absentee, zamindars are well-documented consequences of the Permanent Settlement.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Naoroji's estimate of the 'drain' included only direct government remittances (Home Charges) and excluded private remittances by British individuals and companies. 2. Critics of the Drain Theory argued that some of these remittances represented legitimate payment for capital and services (e.g., interest on productive investment) rather than pure exploitation. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 2 correctly reflects a common counter-argument that part of the drain represented returns to capital/services. Statement 1 is incorrect - Naoroji's broader conception of the drain also included private remittances/profits repatriated by British individuals and companies, not just Home Charges.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Deccan Riots Commission (1878) recommended legislative protection for peasants against unscrupulous moneylenders. 2. This recommendation led to the enactment of the Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Act. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct: the Deccan Riots Commission's findings on rural indebtedness led to the Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Act, 1879, aimed at restricting moneylenders' powers.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Under Mahalwari settlement, the co-parcenary village community as a whole was held responsible for the revenue, distinguishing it from both Zamindari and Ryotwari systems. 2. Mahalwari was applied uniformly with identical revenue rates across all regions where it operated, unlike the regionally varied Ryotwari rates. 3. In practice, a village headman (lambardar) often collected dues from individual cultivators on behalf of the mahal. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false - Mahalwari revenue rates and assessment periods varied considerably across regions and settlements, not uniformly applied.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. William Digby and other contemporary critics argued that famine mortality was worsened by continued grain exports from India during famine years. 2. The colonial government's non-interventionist stance during early famines was influenced by laissez-faire economic doctrines then prevalent in Britain. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct: critics like William Digby highlighted continued grain exports amid famine, and the government's reluctance to intervene reflected the influence of laissez-faire economic orthodoxy of the period.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. R.C. Dutt's 'Economic History of India' was presented, in part, as an appeal to the British Parliament regarding Indian economic distress. 2. Dutt served in the Indian Civil Service before becoming a prominent economic critic of British policy. 3. Dutt attributed recurring famines primarily to over-population rather than to revenue and economic policy. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct - Dutt was an ICS officer and addressed his critique partly to Parliament. Statement 3 is false: Dutt attributed famines primarily to excessive land revenue demand and impoverishment caused by British economic policy, not overpopulation.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The 'guarantee system' of railway finance meant that risk of loss was substantially borne by Indian taxpayers while profits accrued largely to British shareholders. 2. Railways facilitated famine relief by enabling faster movement of grain to famine-affected regions in later famines compared to earlier ones. 3. Railway construction had no linkage to opening up new areas for cash-crop cultivation for export. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false - railway expansion was closely linked to opening the hinterland for export-oriented cash-crop cultivation (cotton, wheat, oilseeds), a core nationalist critique of railway priorities.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Naoroji, Dutt and Ranade are collectively regarded as pioneers of the 'economic nationalism' school before the emergence of Gandhian economic thought. 2. All three uniformly rejected any role for the state in promoting industrialization, favouring pure private enterprise. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is false - Ranade, in particular, strongly advocated state-aided industrialization, differing from a purely laissez-faire private-enterprise approach.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements regarding the Champaran indigo system: 1. Under 'tinkathia', peasants were forced to cultivate indigo on 3/20th of their land. 2. Falling indigo prices due to competition from synthetic (German) dyes led planters to try to extract cash 'compensation' from tenants in lieu of the indigo obligation, sparking fresh discontent before 1917. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct: the fraction was 3/20th of holding, and the collapse of natural indigo prices due to synthetic dye competition led planters to impose illegal cash exactions, deepening peasant grievances addressed by Gandhi's Champaran enquiry.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Charter Act of 1833 ended the East India Company's remaining commercial functions, turning it into a purely administrative body. 2. This shift is linked by economic historians to a more systematic exploitation of India as a market for British manufactures and source of raw materials, rather than a trading post. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct: the Charter Act of 1833 stripped the Company of trading rights, aligning colonial administration more directly with metropolitan industrial and commercial interests.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The 'drain of wealth' concept has been critiqued by some later economic historians for overstating the drain's magnitude relative to India's total output. 2. Nonetheless, most scholars agree that some net unilateral transfer of resources from India to Britain did occur under colonial rule. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements reflect the balanced historiographical position - the precise magnitude of the drain remains debated, but the existence of a net unilateral resource transfer from India to Britain is widely accepted.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Under Ryotwari, land could be sold, mortgaged or transferred by the peasant proprietor, unlike under a purely occupancy-tenant arrangement. 2. This transferability, combined with revenue demand pressure, sometimes contributed to peasant indebtedness and land alienation to moneylenders. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct - Ryotwari conferred quasi-proprietary, transferable rights, which under revenue pressure and indebtedness sometimes led to land alienation to non-cultivating moneylenders, especially evident in the Deccan.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Famine Codes developed after 1880 introduced classification of famine severity and prescribed relief works and gratuitous relief measures. 2. Despite the Famine Codes, mortality during the famine of 1899-1900 was lower than during the famine of 1876-78 due to improved relief administration and railway-assisted grain movement. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are broadly correct: the Famine Codes systematized relief classification, and improved railway-based grain distribution and relief administration are credited with somewhat reducing (though not eliminating) mortality in later famines compared to 1876-78.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Naoroji's parliamentary election in 1892 was significant partly because it gave him a platform in Britain to raise Indian economic grievances directly. 2. He contested and won as an independent candidate with no party affiliation. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is false - Naoroji contested and won as a Liberal Party candidate from Finsbury Central, not as an independent.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The commercialization of agriculture led to regional specialization, e.g., Punjab in wheat, Bengal in jute, and parts of Deccan/Berar in cotton. 2. This regional specialization made local food security more, rather than less, vulnerable to crop failure or price crashes in the specialized cash crop. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct: regional crop specialization (wheat in Punjab, jute in Bengal, cotton in Deccan/Berar) increased dependence on single crops, heightening vulnerability to price crashes and food shortages.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Both the Permanent Settlement and the Ryotwari system were introduced with the explicit aim of maximizing long-term agricultural investment by cultivators. 2. The Permanent Settlement's fixed demand meant the state could not benefit from future increases in agricultural output/prices, a limitation later administrators sought to avoid in Ryotwari and Mahalwari. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 2 is correct - later systems deliberately allowed periodic revenue revision to let the state capture rising output/prices. Statement 1 is incorrect for the Permanent Settlement, whose primary rationale was administrative simplicity and assured revenue for the state, not maximizing cultivator investment (a claimed benefit that mostly failed to materialize).

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Rice and wheat exports from India increased continuously and without exception throughout the entire colonial period. 2. India, despite exporting agricultural cash crops, occasionally imported food grains during acute famine years. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 2 is correct - food grain imports occurred at times, especially during severe famine emergencies. Statement 1 is an overgeneralization and incorrect, as food-grain export volumes fluctuated across the period rather than rising continuously without exception.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Champaran Agrarian Act (1917-18), enacted after Gandhi's inquiry, abolished the tinkathia system. 2. This is regarded as one of the first legislative outcomes directly traceable to a Gandhi-led movement in India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct: the Champaran Agrarian Act abolished the tinkathia system, marking one of the earliest tangible legislative successes of a Gandhi-led campaign in India.

basic.q: The Regulating Act of 1773 created the post of Governor-General of which Presidency, to be assisted by an Executive Council?
basic.e: The Regulating Act, 1773 created the office of Governor-General of Bengal (Warren Hastings was the first), with an Executive Council of four members.

basic.q: The Regulating Act of 1773 provided for the establishment of a Supreme Court at which city?
basic.e: The Act provided for a Supreme Court at Calcutta (established 1774), with a Chief Justice and three other judges.

basic.q: Pitt's India Act of 1784 established which body to control the East India Company's political affairs, marking the beginning of dual government?
basic.e: Pitt's India Act, 1784 established the Board of Control in London to supervise the Company's political/civil/military affairs, initiating a system of dual government (Company + Crown control).

basic.q: The Charter Act of 1813 ended the East India Company's monopoly over trade with India, while retaining its monopoly over trade with which country?
basic.e: The Charter Act of 1813 threw open trade with India to all British subjects but retained the Company's monopoly over the China trade and trade in tea.

basic.q: The Charter Act of 1813 earmarked a sum of Rs 1 lakh annually for which purpose?
basic.e: The Act set aside Rs 1 lakh per annum for the revival and promotion of education/literature, an early step toward state involvement in Indian education.

basic.q: The Charter Act of 1833 designated the Governor-General of Bengal as the:
o: President of the Board of Control
basic.e: The Charter Act of 1833 created the office of Governor-General of India (first holder: Lord William Bentinck), centralizing legislative authority over all British India.

basic.q: The Charter Act of 1833 provided for the addition of a Law Member to the Governor-General's Council; the first person to hold this post was:
basic.e: Lord Macaulay was the first Law Member added to the Governor-General's Council under the Charter Act of 1833.

basic.q: The Charter Act of 1853 introduced open competitive examinations for recruitment to which service?
basic.e: The Charter Act of 1853 introduced open competition as the basis for recruitment to the Indian Civil Service, ending patronage-based nomination.

basic.q: The Government of India Act, 1858, enacted after the Revolt of 1857, resulted in which major change?
o: Grant of full self-government (Dominion Status) to India
Transfer of power from the East India Company to the British Crown
Introduction of adult franchise for legislative councils
Creation of the Indian National Congress
basic.e: The GoI Act, 1858 ended East India Company rule and transferred governance of India directly to the British Crown, with a Secretary of State for India replacing the Board of Control/Court of Directors.

basic.q: Who became the first Viceroy of India following the Government of India Act, 1858?
basic.e: Lord Canning, already Governor-General, became the first Viceroy of India under the 1858 Act.

basic.q: The Indian Councils Act of 1861 introduced which new feature in the legislative process?
o: Direct election of Indian members to the central legislature
The portfolio system and association of Indians as non-official members in the Legislative Council
basic.e: The Indian Councils Act, 1861 introduced the portfolio system and, for the first time, allowed Indians (as non-official members) to be nominated to the Viceroy's Legislative Council.

basic.q: The Indian Councils Act of 1892 expanded the functions of legislative councils to include:
o: Discussion of the budget and posing of questions to the executive
basic.e: The Indian Councils Act, 1892 allowed council members to discuss the budget and ask questions, though voting on budgetary matters was not permitted.

basic.q: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) is particularly notable for introducing:
basic.e: The 1909 Act introduced separate electorates for Muslims, institutionalizing communal representation in Indian legislative politics.

basic.q: The Government of India Act, 1919, based on the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms, introduced 'dyarchy' at which level of government?
basic.e: The GoI Act, 1919 introduced dyarchy (dual government) at the provincial level, dividing subjects into 'transferred' and 'reserved' categories.

basic.q: The Government of India Act, 1935, provided for the introduction of:
o: Provincial autonomy and an All-India Federation (never fully implemented)
Dyarchy at the provincial level for the first time
Separate electorates for the first time
basic.e: The GoI Act, 1935 provided for provincial autonomy (replacing dyarchy at the provincial level) and proposed an All-India Federation including princely states, which never came into force due to lack of accession by enough princely states.

basic.q: The Government of India Act, 1935 provided for the establishment of which judicial institution, inaugurated in 1937?
basic.e: The Federal Court of India, established under the 1935 Act, was inaugurated in 1937 and functioned as a precursor to the post-independence Supreme Court.

basic.q: Under the Government of India Act, 1858, the Secretary of State for India was assisted by a body called the:
basic.e: The Secretary of State for India was assisted by the Council of India, a body of experienced members based in London.

basic.q: The Charter Act of 1853 gave the Legislative Council of the Governor-General a distinct character, often described as a:
basic.e: The 1853 Act enlarged and gave a more parliamentary character to the Legislative Council by adding additional members for legislative purposes, earning it the description of a 'mini-Parliament'.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements about the Regulating Act, 1773: 1. It made the Bombay and Madras Presidencies subordinate to the Governor-General of Bengal in matters of war, revenue and diplomacy. 2. It prohibited Company servants from engaging in private trade and from accepting bribes/presents from Indians. 3. It established the Board of Control in London. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong - the Board of Control was established later, by Pitt's India Act of 1784, not the Regulating Act.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Pitt's India Act, 1784 established a system in which the Company retained control over commercial affairs while the Crown (via the Board of Control) supervised political affairs. 2. This dual system of control continued essentially unchanged until 1858. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct: Pitt's India Act established the dual-government structure (Company for commerce, Crown/Board of Control for politics), which persisted with modifications until the GoI Act of 1858 ended Company rule entirely.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements about the Charter Acts: 1. The Charter Act of 1793 primarily renewed the Company's charter for a further 20 years without major structural change. 2. The Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company's trade monopoly with India but retained its administrative and political authority. 3. The Charter Act of 1833 ended the Company's remaining commercial functions altogether. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: All three statements correctly summarize the progression: 1793 was largely a renewal, 1813 opened trade but kept administration, and 1833 stripped the Company of all commercial activity, making it a purely administrative body.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Charter Act of 1813 for the first time permitted Christian missionaries to propagate their faith in India. 2. It also asserted the sovereignty of the British Crown over the Company's Indian territories. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct - the 1813 Act permitted missionary activity and explicitly asserted Crown sovereignty over Company-held Indian territories.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Charter Act of 1833 vested legislative power exclusively in the Governor-General-in-Council, superseding the legislative powers earlier held by Madras and Bombay. 2. It opened Company services to Indians in theory, without discrimination based on religion, birth or colour. 3. It fully implemented open, merit-based recruitment for all covenanted civil service posts. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false - although the 1833 Act declared no Indian would be debarred from office on grounds of religion/birth/colour, in practice few Indians entered the covenanted civil service; open competitive recruitment came only with the 1853 Act.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Charter Act of 1853 separated, for the first time, the legislative and executive functions of the Governor-General's Council. 2. It also introduced, for the first time, representation of Indians in the Legislative Council. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is false - Indian representation in the legislative council came later (the 1861 Act introduced Indian non-official members), not in 1853.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Government of India Act, 1858 replaced the Court of Directors and Board of Control with a Secretary of State for India assisted by a Council. 2. It abolished the office of Governor-General, replacing it entirely with a new office titled Viceroy with no continuity of personnel. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is misleading/false - the Governor-General's office continued, merely acquiring the additional title of Viceroy; Lord Canning, the sitting Governor-General, simply became the first Viceroy, showing continuity, not replacement.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Indian Councils Act of 1861 restored legislative powers to the Bombay and Madras Presidencies, which had been curtailed since 1833. 2. It also allowed the Governor-General to issue ordinances in emergencies. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct: the 1861 Act restored provincial legislative councils in Bombay and Madras (and provided for new ones elsewhere) and empowered the Governor-General to promulgate ordinances during emergencies.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Indian Councils Act of 1892 introduced the principle of indirect election, though the term 'election' was not officially used. 2. Under this Act, non-official members could be recommended by bodies such as universities, district boards and chambers of commerce. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct: the 1892 Act introduced a limited, indirect form of election (termed 'nomination on recommendation') through bodies like universities and chambers of commerce, without formally legalizing elections.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements comparing the Indian Councils Acts of 1892 and 1909: 1. The 1892 Act allowed budget discussion without voting rights; the 1909 Act expanded this to allow moving resolutions on the budget. 2. The 1909 Act introduced separate electorates, a feature absent in the 1892 Act. 3. The 1909 Act allowed for the first time an Indian to be appointed to the Viceroy's Executive Council. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: All three statements are correct: the 1909 Act expanded budgetary powers, introduced separate electorates, and Satyendra Prasad Sinha became the first Indian appointed to the Viceroy's Executive Council around this period.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act, 1919: 1. It divided provincial subjects into 'transferred' subjects administered by ministers responsible to the legislature, and 'reserved' subjects controlled by the Governor and his executive council. 2. It introduced direct elections to the legislatures for the first time on a limited franchise. 3. It also created a bicameral central legislature comprising the Council of State and the Legislative Assembly. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: All three statements correctly describe the 1919 Act: the transferred/reserved division of dyarchy, introduction of direct elections on limited franchise, and creation of a bicameral central legislature.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Dyarchy under the 1919 Act was applied at the provincial level only. 2. The Government of India Act, 1935 extended a similar dual arrangement (dyarchy) to the centre while granting full autonomy to the provinces. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct: dyarchy operated at the provincial level under 1919, whereas the 1935 Act shifted the dyarchical arrangement to the centre (for the proposed federation) while provinces gained full autonomy.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The federal scheme envisaged by the Government of India Act, 1935 required a specified number of princely states to accede before it could come into force. 2. Due to insufficient accession, the federal part of the Act never came into effect, though the provincial autonomy part did. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct: the federation required princely states representing a certain proportion of population/seats to join, which never materialized, so only the provincial autonomy provisions took effect (from 1937).

intermediate.q: Arrange the following constitutional developments in chronological order: 1. Introduction of separate electorates 2. Establishment of the Federal Court 3. Introduction of dyarchy in provinces 4. Government of India transferred from Company to Crown
intermediate.e: Correct order: Crown takeover (1858) then separate electorates (1909) then provincial dyarchy (1919) then Federal Court established (1937, under the 1935 Act).

intermediate.q: Which of the following Act-feature pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Government of India Act, 1935 - Provincial autonomy
Indian Councils Act, 1861 - Introduction of dyarchy
Charter Act, 1853 - Open competitive examination for ICS
Indian Councils Act, 1909 - Separate electorates for Muslims
intermediate.e: Dyarchy was introduced by the Government of India Act, 1919, not the Indian Councils Act of 1861, which is known instead for the portfolio system and restoring provincial legislative councils.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Charter Act of 1853, unlike earlier Charter Acts, did not specify a fixed term of years for renewal of the Company's role. 2. This effectively meant the British Parliament could review the Company's administration at any time, contributing to the eventual takeover in 1858. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct: unlike previous Charter Acts (with fixed 20-year renewal terms), the 1853 Act left the Company's tenure open-ended, subject to Parliament's discretion, which facilitated the transition to Crown rule after 1857.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Under the 1935 Act, the Federal Legislature was to be bicameral, comprising a Council of State and a Federal Assembly. 2. Under the same Act, provincial legislatures in some provinces were also made bicameral for the first time. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct: the 1935 Act proposed a bicameral federal legislature and also allowed bicameralism in larger provinces such as Bengal, Bombay, Madras, Bihar, Assam and the United Provinces.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Indian Councils Act, 1909 retained an official majority in the central Legislative Council while allowing a non-official majority in provincial councils. 2. This meant that even after 1909, the Government of India could not be outvoted at the centre, unlike in some provinces. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct: the 1909 Act preserved an official majority at the centre while permitting non-official majorities in provincial councils, ensuring the central government could not be outvoted.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Regulating Act, 1773 required the Governor-General-in-Council to send regular reports on revenue, civil and military affairs to the Company's Court of Directors in London. 2. It also, for the first time, allowed the British Crown to appoint the Governor-General directly, bypassing the Company's Court of Directors. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is false - under the Regulating Act, the Governor-General and Council were named in the Act itself and subsequently appointed by the Company's Court of Directors, subject to Crown approval, not directly appointed by the Crown.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Regulating Act, 1773 is generally regarded as the first attempt by the British Parliament to regulate and control the affairs of the East India Company through statute. 2. However, the Act failed to clearly demarcate the respective jurisdictions of the Supreme Court and the Governor-General-in-Council, leading to conflicts, most notably in the Patna Case and the Raja Nandakumar case. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct: the Regulating Act was Parliament's first statutory intervention, and ambiguity in dividing authority between the Supreme Court and the Governor-General's Council caused notable jurisdictional conflicts, exemplified by the Patna and Nandakumar cases.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Pitt's India Act, 1784 gave the Board of Control the power to 'superintend, direct and control' all acts relating to civil, military and revenue affairs of the Company in India. 2. It reduced the Governor-General's Council from four to three members, giving the Governor-General a casting vote in case of a tie. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct: the Board of Control was granted sweeping supervisory power, and the Governor-General's Council strength was reduced to three, with the Governor-General given a casting vote.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Charter Act of 1833 is significant for proposing, in principle, equality of opportunity for Indians in Company services regardless of religion, place of birth, descent or colour. 2. It is also notable for centralizing all legislative power in British India in the Governor-General-in-Council, making the Bombay and Madras governments merely executive, not legislative, bodies. 3. Despite these provisions, the Act made no changes to the method of appointing the Law Member of the Council. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false - the 1833 Act itself created the new post of Law Member, a change in the composition of the Council rather than 'no change'.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Charter Act of 1853 was the last of the series of Charter Acts and did not renew the Company's rule for a fixed further term, unlike previous Acts. 2. It increased the number of members in the Governor-General's Legislative Council for legislative purposes by adding representatives nominated from certain provinces. 3. It abolished the Company's patronage over civil service appointments in favour of open competition, effective immediately and equally in Britain and India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 overstates the case - while open competition was introduced for the Indian Civil Service, examinations were held only in England, effectively still limiting Indian entry due to age, cost and location barriers, not an equal 'immediate' opportunity in both countries.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Government of India Act, 1858 did not immediately grant any additional political rights to Indians; its primary effect was a change in the apex structure of control from Company to Crown. 2. Queen Victoria's Proclamation of 1858, issued around the same time, promised non-interference in religious matters and equal treatment of Indians in government service, in principle. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct: the 1858 Act mainly restructured control from Company to Crown, while the accompanying Queen's Proclamation made symbolic promises of religious non-interference and equal treatment, though these often remained unfulfilled in practice.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Indian Councils Act, 1861 empowered the Governor-General to create new provinces and appoint Lieutenant-Governors for them. 2. It also allowed the Governor-General's Legislative Council to make laws for the whole of British India, including the Presidencies. 3. It fully excluded any legislative role for the Bombay and Madras Presidencies. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false - the 1861 Act actually restored legislative councils to Bombay and Madras and enabled new ones (Bengal 1862, NWP 1886, Punjab 1897), rather than excluding them.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Indian Councils Act, 1892 increased the number of additional (non-official) members in the central and provincial legislative councils compared to 1861. 2. It empowered legislative councils to reject the annual financial statement (budget) if a majority of non-official members voted against it. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is false - the councils under the 1892 Act could only discuss the budget and ask questions; they had no power to vote on or reject it.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Morley-Minto Reforms (1909) are sometimes viewed by historians as an attempt to use constitutional concessions to counter the growing influence of the Extremist/Swadeshi movement within the Congress. 2. The separate electorate provision for Muslims under this Act was demanded through the Simla Deputation of 1906. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct: the 1909 reforms are seen partly as a response to rising nationalist militancy post-Partition of Bengal, and the demand for separate electorates was voiced by the Simla Deputation (1906), subsequently formalized in the Act.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Under the Government of India Act, 1919, 'reserved' subjects in the provinces (like law and order, finance) remained under the Governor and executive councillors not responsible to the legislature. 2. 'Transferred' subjects (like education, health, local self-government) were administered by ministers responsible to the legislature. 3. At the centre, the same transferred-reserved dyarchical division was applied to central subjects as well. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false - dyarchy under the 1919 Act applied only at the provincial level; the centre had a different, non-dyarchical structure with the Viceroy's Executive Council remaining largely unaccountable to the legislature.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Government of India Act, 1935 abolished the Council of India that had assisted the Secretary of State since 1858. 2. It provided for the creation of a Federal Court and a Federal Railway Authority. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct: the 1935 Act abolished the Council of India (the Secretary of State would instead have advisers), and it provided for a Federal Court and a Federal Railway Authority as part of the federal scheme.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Provincial autonomy under the 1935 Act meant provinces were no longer subordinate to the Government of India in their assigned sphere. 2.
